recognize_zh: 兩顆分節中性球（紅色箭頭）細胞質邊緣各有淡藍灰色的小斑塊，即杜勒小體（Döhle bodies）；細胞質顆粒並未變粗、也沒有空泡，所以沒有毒性變化。
features: Two segmented neutrophils with small pale blue-gray cytoplasmic patches at the periphery (arrows)
Neutrophil cytoplasm otherwise pale with normal fine granulation; no toxic granulation or vacuolization
Background red cells with rouleaux-like stacking and overlapping in a thick area of the smear
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, in a relatively thick area, shows two segmented neutrophils each containing a small, pale blue-gray peripheral cytoplasmic inclusion consistent with a Döhle body. The neutrophils lack toxic granulation and cytoplasmic vacuolization. Red cells are overlapping; platelets are present. Findings are consistent with Döhle bodies without accompanying toxic changes, which may be seen in pregnancy, burns, G-CSF therapy or early infection; if inclusions are large and present in all neutrophils with thrombocytopenia and giant platelets, MYH9-related disorder should be considered.

ddx.vs: May-Hegglin inclusions are larger, more spindle-shaped, present in nearly all granulocytes and accompanied by giant platelets and thrombocytopenia.
Sepsis-related Döhle bodies are usually accompanied by toxic granulation and cytoplasmic vacuoles, which are absent here.
Chédiak-Higashi granules are giant, dense azurophilic/peroxidase-positive granules rather than pale blue-gray patches.
